On 31 March 1917 Denmark handed its Caribbean islands, St Thomas, St John and St Croix, to the United States, which paid 25 million dollars in gold. They became the US Virgin Islands.

The United States wanted the harbour of St Thomas to guard the approaches to the new Panama Canal and feared that Germany might seize the islands in World War I. Danish voters approved the sale in a referendum in 1916; the islanders were not asked.

The navy ran the islands until 1931. Islanders became US citizens in 1927 and elected their own governor from 1970, but still cannot vote for president. Tourism replaced sugar, the old base of the Danish West Indies.
sum: On 31 March 1917 Denmark handed its Caribbean islands, St Thomas, St John and St Croix, to the United States, which paid 25 million dollars in gold. They became the US Virgin Islands.
